title: HL vs SL Revision Needs: Why One Plan Fails
summary: Understand HL vs SL revision needs, from syllabus depth and paper structure to time pressure, then build a smarter IB revision approach for each level.
body_markdown:
**HL vs SL revision needs are not identical.** Higher Level subjects generally require broader coverage, deeper connections, and greater endurance in demanding tasks. Standard Level subjects involve less prescribed teaching time, but they still require precise knowledge, effective exam technique, and disciplined pacing.


The best IB revision approach uses the same foundation for both levels: active recall, question practice, feedback, and retesting. You then adjust the time allocation, difficulty, and type of practice according to each subject's syllabus and assessment structure.


### The official IB distinction between HL and SL


The IB recommends **240 teaching hours for an HL subject** and **150 teaching hours for an SL subject** . HL therefore has about 1.6 times the recommended teaching time, reflecting greater breadth, depth, or both.


However, SL is not simply an easier or diluted version of HL. Both levels are academically demanding, and the precise difference depends on the subject. HL may add content, an extra paper, longer examinations, more sophisticated methods, or higher expectations for analysis and synthesis.


Students normally take three HL subjects, with a fourth permitted, and take their remaining subjects at SL. Your current subject guide and assessment outline should determine your revision priorities because the HL-SL distinction is not identical across the Diploma Programme.


Revision factor Typical SL need Typical HL need


Syllabus coverage Secure the complete defined course Master the core plus additional content or extensions


Depth Explain and apply ideas accurately Connect ideas and handle unfamiliar contexts


Paper practice Train the exact SL components Prepare for longer, additional, or more demanding tasks


Time pressure Protect marks through reliable pacing Maintain accuracy across complex, extended work


Error review Correct factual and technique gaps Repair weak conceptual links and reasoning chains


### How HL and SL demands differ in practice


### HL usually requires greater breadth and depth


At SL, complete command of the assessed syllabus is usually more valuable than exploring a few topics beyond the course requirements. Students should retrieve essential knowledge, interpret command terms correctly, and execute recurring question types reliably.


HL requires that foundation plus another layer. Depending on the subject, this may involve additional topics, extended texts, sophisticated methods, stronger evaluation, or connections between several concepts. Memorizing isolated facts is especially risky because unfamiliar questions expose weak conceptual links.


For example, an SL science student might explain a process and interpret familiar data. An HL student may need to combine that process with additional content, analyse an unfamiliar situation, and justify a conclusion through several stages of reasoning.


### Paper structures can differ substantially


There is no universal rule that every HL course has an additional paper. Check the current official subject brief rather than relying on advice for another subject or an earlier syllabus.


In[Mathematics: Analysis and Approaches](https://ibo.org/contentassets/5895a05412144fe890312bad52b17044/subject-brief-dp-math-analysis-and-approaches-en.pdf) , SL has two external papers of **1.5 hours each** . HL has two **2-hour** papers and a **1-hour Paper 3** containing compulsory extended problem-solving questions. Repeating only SL-style questions would leave an important HL assessment mode underprepared.


The current[IB Biology subject brief](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/recognition/pdfs/dp_sciences_biology_subject-brief_jan_2022_e.pdf) , first assessed in 2025, uses a different structure. Both levels have Paper 1 and Paper 2, but total external assessment time is **3 hours at SL** and **4.5 hours at HL** . HL students consequently need broader retrieval and greater concentration across the assessment.


Differences may also be qualitative. The[IB Language B subject brief](https://ibo.org/contentassets/5895a05412144fe890312bad52b17044/lang-b-2018-en.pdf) gives SL and HL the same broad assessment outline, but HL tasks require greater linguistic complexity and higher-order thinking. HL students also study two literary works, and the oral stimulus differs by level.


### Time pressure involves more than paper length


A longer HL paper does not necessarily provide more breathing room. Pressure depends on marks, reading load, decision-making, and the number of connected steps required. HL practice must therefore develop **cognitive endurance** , not merely the ability to solve isolated difficult questions.


SL students face a different risk: assuming a shorter paper is forgiving. One overlong response or stalled calculation can consume a substantial proportion of the available time. Timed SL practice should build quick recognition, reliable pacing, and the discipline to move on.


The[RevisionDojo guide to mock exams](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/revisiondojo-mock-exams) explains how realistic simulations and question-level review can reveal both knowledge gaps and pacing problems.


### How revision should change by level


### Prioritize complete and efficient coverage at SL


Begin with a syllabus audit, labelling each topic secure, uncertain, or weak. Repair weak areas with a brief explanation followed immediately by questions rather than repeatedly rereading a whole chapter.


A focused SL session might include:


- **10 minutes** of active recall for definitions, formulas, quotations, or processes
- **25-35 minutes** of topic-specific questions
- **10 minutes** of marking and error classification
- A short retest several days later


Once coverage is secure, introduce mixed questions and timed sections. Mixed practice forces you to identify the relevant method without being told which topic is being tested. The[RevisionDojo active recall guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/active-recall-for-ib-the-only-method-you-need) explains how to replace passive review with retrieval.


### Build connections and transfer at HL


HL revision needs an additional cycle after basic recall: **combine, apply, justify, and evaluate** . Practise questions that mix topics, require extended reasoning, or present information in unfamiliar forms. In essay subjects, this could mean integrating evidence and reaching a qualified judgment instead of reproducing a memorized response.


An HL session might include:


- **10 minutes** retrieving prerequisite knowledge
- **15-20 minutes** repairing one difficult concept
- **30-45 minutes** completing demanding or mixed-topic questions
- **15 minutes** analysing the reasoning behind lost marks
- A later retest using a different question on the same skill


Use the[RevisionDojo IB resources hub](https://www.revisiondojo.com/ib) to locate level-appropriate material. Jojo AI can clarify a difficult step, but attempt the problem first and then return to independent work so that the explanation becomes usable knowledge.


### Allocate time using evidence


The **240:150 teaching-hour ratio** suggests that HL usually deserves a larger revision budget, but it is not an official formula for independent study. A weak, heavily assessed SL subject may need more attention this week than a secure HL subject.


Assign time using four variables:


1. **Scope:** How much assessed content remains insecure?
2. **Performance:** What do recent tests and timed attempts show?
3. **Assessment demand:** Which paper styles require more training?
4. **Urgency:** Which examination or deadline comes first?


Give HL subjects more total time as a starting point, then adjust weekly. Never reduce SL to occasional flashcards simply because of its label. An SL 7 contributes **7 points** to the diploma score, just as an HL 7 does.


### Build a level-sensitive weekly plan


List every paper you will sit, including its duration, weighting, question types, permitted materials, and your current weakness. The official[IB overview of SL and HL](https://www.ibo.org/globalassets/new-structure/programmes/dp/pdfs/slhl-brief-en.pdf) and current subject briefs provide the authoritative starting point.


A balanced week could include:


- **HL subjects:** two depth or application blocks and one timed block for the highest-priority paper
- **SL subjects:** one coverage block and one question-practice block, with timed sections rotated across subjects
- **Daily recall:** short mixed retrieval for knowledge-heavy courses at both levels
- **Weekly review:** changes based on marks, timing, repeated errors, and unfinished targets


Progress from topic questions to timed sections and then full papers. The[RevisionDojo past-paper timetable guide](https://www.revisiondojo.com/blog/ib-exam-revision-timetable-past-papers) shows how to combine diagnosis, repair, integration, and simulation instead of leaving all timed work until the final weeks.


### Common mistakes when revising HL and SL


**Giving every subject equal time** ignores differences in performance, scope, paper length, and urgency. Maintain weekly contact with every subject, but allocate additional time where evidence shows it is needed.


**Using HL resources for SL without checking scope** can waste time and encourage irrelevant detail. SL students should master their own syllabus before studying extensions.


**Treating HL as a larger memorization task** produces fragile knowledge. HL students need transfer, comparison, synthesis, evaluation, and multi-step reasoning as well as retrieval.


**Practising topics but not papers** neglects pacing, selection, endurance, and recovery after difficult questions. Both levels need timed work, although HL students may require earlier stamina training.


**Measuring progress only in hours** rewards activity rather than improvement. Track questions completed, topics secured, repeated errors, timing checkpoints, and later retest results.


### Conclusion


HL and SL subjects share the need for accurate knowledge, active recall, exam practice, and honest feedback. Their priorities differ because HL commonly adds breadth, depth, complex application, or longer assessment demands, while SL rewards complete coverage and consistent execution within its syllabus.


Build one revision system, then vary its workload, question difficulty, and paper practice by level and current performance. RevisionDojo can support this with Questionbank practice, Study Notes, Flashcards, Jojo AI explanations, and Mock Exams.
